pr_title: Garbage collect asynchronously in the WAL Watcher
pr_body:
The WAL Watcher replays a checkpoint after it is created in order to
garbage collect series that no longer exist in the WAL. Currently the
garbage collection process is done serially with reading from the tip of
the WAL which can cause large delays in writing samples to remote
storage just after compaction occurs.

This also fixes a memory leak where dropped series are not cleaned up as
part of the SeriesReset process.

Closes #6007 

cc: @cstyan @tomwilkie
pr_comments:

issue_context.title: Remote write backs up during compaction
issue_context.body:
## Bug Report
**What did you do?**
Ran remote_write code.

**What did you expect to see?**
Continuous sending of samples to remote storage.

**What did you see instead? Under which circumstances?**
During a compaction samples will backup causing a several minute delay in some cases.

![CompactionRWLag](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3280472/64627253-858da900-d3ac-11e9-8672-fde629ea4a64.png)

**Environment**

* System information: Docker/Kubernetes
* Prometheus version: v2.12.0
comments: Did you have enough cores for all of it?

> Did you have enough cores for all of it?

Yes, that Prometheus has a large amount of CPU allocated to it and is not significantly CPU throttled during compaction. Also, if it was throttled I would expect some requests to still make it out, it looks like in my case no requests are being sent for a significant amount of time.

![NoRemoteSends](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3280472/64637105-597c2300-d3c0-11e9-8da2-b55f13381019.png)

Hoping to dig in a bit more soon.
